::: {.why}
The return you earn if nothing moves, which sounds trivial and turns out to be one of the few signals with a consistent definition and a consistent premium across markets.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the single definition of carry that specialises correctly to bonds, currencies, commodities and equity index futures.
- Build a carry signal on the instruments you have and report its correlation with your trend signals.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write the general definition: carry is the return from holding the asset assuming the price is unchanged, which for a futures curve is the slope between the front and next contract, for a currency is the interest rate differential, and for a bond is the yield plus rolldown. Check your four sentences from last night against it and fix the one that was wrong.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build and evaluate it: a carry signal from the term structure of whatever instruments you have, cross-sectionally ranked across instruments. Report its Sharpe, its correlation with trend, and the Sharpe of the two combined. Carry and trend are close to uncorrelated and that is why they appear together in every managed futures product.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
A carry signal built from term structure joins the book, evaluated on the same footing as everything else, with its correlation to trend measured so the combination in week 29 has a real input.
:::

Give the one definition of carry that works for bonds, currencies and commodity futures, and apply it to each in a sentence.
